record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: Current crisp similarity languages reason with exact numerical distance values. Develop logical formalisms for metric or distance reasoning that can handle approximate or uncertain distances, for example by incorporating vagueness, fuzzy truth values, or probabilistic information.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Standard "similarity" or "distance" modal/first-order languages for metric spaces are crisp: their formulas are evaluated in a metric space (X, d) and refer to exact numerical thresholds, e.g. via operators such as ∃^{≤a}φ ("there exists a point at distance at most a satisfying φ") or comparative-similarity predicates of the form "y is at least as close to x as z is", with truth values in {0,1}.

Design a logical formalism for reasoning about metric (or, more generally, distance) spaces in which distances themselves, or the truth values of distance assertions, may be approximate or uncertain. Concretely, propose a syntax and a semantics — over a class of distance structures (X, d) possibly enriched with a probability measure, a fuzzy similarity relation, or a vagueness/tolerance structure — satisfying the following requirements:

1. The language should contain analogues of the crisp distance/similarity operators (such as ∃^{≤a}, ∀^{≤a}, or comparative-closeness predicates), but with truth values taken in a suitable algebra (e.g. the real interval [0,1] under a t-norm, a probability algebra, or a many-valued algebra modelling vagueness) so that formulas can express graded, fuzzy, or probabilistic distance statements (for instance, "φ holds with high probability at some nearby point" or "x is approximately as close to y as to z").

2. Give a precise model-theoretic semantics interpreting the language in the chosen class of uncertain distance structures.

3. Investigate the resulting logic: in particular, axiomatize it (sound and complete deductive calculus) and determine the decidability and computational complexity of its satisfiability/validity problem.

The task is to develop such a formalism, or to prove that any reasonable formalism meeting these criteria must fail one of the desired meta-properties (e.g. recursive axiomatizability or decidability).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a programmatic open problem asking for the development of logics for metric/distance reasoning with uncertainty. While various related formalisms exist — fuzzy modal logics for similarity reasoning, probabilistic metric spaces, behavioural (pseudo)metrics with characteristic quantitative modal logics, and similarity-based fuzzy metric spaces — no single accepted formalism has been developed that subsumes the crisp similarity/distance modal logics for metric spaces and extends them to vague, fuzzy, or probabilistic distances with a full axiomatization and decidability analysis. The general challenge therefore remains open, although there has been substantial partial progress along each of the suggested directions.

status_evidence.title: A Fuzzy Modal Logic for Similarity Reasoning
status_evidence.snippet: A modal fuzzy logic is proposed with semantics based on Kripke structures where the accessibility relations are fuzzy similarity relations measuring how similar are the possible worlds.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: fuzzy modal logics for similarity have been proposed.

status_evidence.title: Characteristic Logics for Behavioural Hemimetrics via Fuzzy Lax Extensions
status_evidence.snippet: For systems involving quantitative data such as transition probabilities, fuzzy truth values, or labellings in metric spaces, it is appropriate to use quantitative measures of behavioural similarity.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative modal logics for behavioural distance have been studied, addressing aspects of the problem.

status_evidence.title: From topology to metric: Modal logic and quantification in metric spaces
status_evidence.snippet: A uniform modal framework for reasoning about topology and relative distance in metric and distance spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Crisp distance modal logics over metric spaces are the established baseline that the open problem proposes to extend.

status_evidence.title: Modal Logics for Metric Spaces: Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems on modal logics for metric spaces, including handling of approximate or uncertain distances.
status_evidence.claim: The development of logics for uncertain distances is listed as an open problem.
